reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the output contract, resource-assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, resource context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and the behavior findings supplied in the resource-review context. I treated the deterministic aggregate as prior context only, considered direct behavior findings whose affectedResources include `ChargeItemDefinition`, and treated shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings as context only because the assigned resource is neither base resource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `ChargeItemDefinition` was trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden for retaining the exact core resource is weak. That materially softens the standards concern around retiring the resource, but it does not erase migration risk where billing rules, applicability expressions, price components, generated APIs, or persisted canonical references were implemented.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes `ChargeItemDefinition` from core, so migration is resource-retirement work; low-cost preservation still matters mainly as successor guidance, terminology compatibility, and explicit transition artifacts.

reasoning.thesisMd: `ChargeItemDefinition` is not a mostly stable resource with a few local breaks. The same-name R6 StructureDefinition and package-index entry are absent, so an R4 instance, canonical reference, generated class, route, operation, or search surface cannot be carried forward as core R6 without an explicit compatibility package or transform. Because the resource was FMM 0/trial-use, the removal can be proportionate, but implementers who used it still need a planned migration rather than field-by-field cleanup.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The dominant migration shape is retired resource identity. The inspected R6 financial surfaces (`Invoice`, `DeviceDefinition.chargeItem`, and `MonetaryComponent`) cover parts of charge or monetary representation, but the reports do not show an official one-to-one successor preserving canonical definition lifecycle, definition-level applicability, property groups, or `ChargeItemDefinition` canonical identity. This makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before individual element preservation can solve much.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource-identity break does lower the leverage of preserving isolated old element names: old instances already fail because the resource type is gone. It does not mean there is no value in avoiding additional breaks. The most useful compatibility work is explicit retirement/successor guidance, optional compatibility packages or aliases where the work group wants transition support, preservation of cheap shared terminology compatibility, and clear REST/search/operation migration policy.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Keeping `ChargeItemDefinition` in R6 core as deprecated would preserve validation, canonical lookup, generated model classes, and resource endpoints, but that is not a clearly low-cost alternative because it keeps a rough FMM 0 billing-definition model in core indefinitely. More targeted lower-cost alternatives remain worth review: publish a formal cross-version map or compatibility IG for applicability/property-group semantics, and if `MonetaryComponent` is an intended target, retain or explicitly map the R4 `deduction` price-component code as a deprecated synonym of `discount`.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings mostly reinforce the same resource-retirement migration: REST endpoint advertisements disappear, resource-specific search surfaces disappear, and the `ChargeItemDefinition/$apply` operation is removed. These are real API/codegen breaks for adopters, but they are largely derivative of removal of a low-maturity resource. The broad base CapabilityStatement system-operation advertisement finding is in scope because it lists `ChargeItemDefinition`, but it needs operation-specific review and does not by itself change the resource conclusion. Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were considered only as background.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's core conclusion: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = Yes`, migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and resource-level posture `migration-program-dominates`. My review adds nuance that the `CONVERSION_OR_MAPPING` finding and the conditional `deduction` terminology narrowing still deserve follow-up because migration dominance is not the same as zero value in standards-compatible transition design.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the R6 ballot package lacks a core `ChargeItemDefinition` resource and that this drives the migration shape. Confidence is lower for replacement intent because the local inputs do not include official R6 narrative, Jira rationale, rendered ballot notes, an official StructureMap/ConceptMap, or full terminology-server expansions.

findingConsiderations.title: ChargeItemDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level fact. An R4 `ChargeItemDefinition` instance and its canonical URL have no same-name R6 core StructureDefinition to validate, resolve, generate, or serve against. Because the R4 artifact is FMM 0/trial-use, removal may be proportionate, but it still makes a migration program unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: No lossless R6 replacement was found for ChargeItemDefinition applicability and property groups
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important standards-review-worthy residual issue. It does not change the fact that the resource is retired, but it shows that migration is not merely a resourceType rename: applicability expressions, property-group conditions, and canonical lifecycle metadata need explicit successor guidance or a compatibility mapping to avoid lossy billing-rule migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Generated R6 models and serializers will not expose ChargeItemDefinition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a high practical impact for adopters because generated SDKs, parsers, schemas, resource enums, and dispatch tables will drop the resource. It is derivative of the resource removal rather than an independent reason to override the resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Potential terminology narrowing when mapping R4 priceComponent.type to R6 MonetaryComponent.type
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This matters only after choosing `MonetaryComponent` or a similar R6 target, so it is not what makes migration unavoidable. It remains a plausible low-cost-to-preserve compatibility issue because keeping `deduction` as a deprecated synonym or publishing an explicit ConceptMap could reduce billing analytics and recoding risk.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the ChargeItemDefinition $apply operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real executable API break for systems that calculated charge-related output through the R4 core operation. Its R4 FMM 0/trial-use status and dependence on the removed resource make it probably proportionate as a core removal, but any migration guide should name the replacement or external IG path rather than leave adopters to infer it.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For `ChargeItemDefinition`, the search break follows from the removed endpoint and resource identity. It reinforces that migration must include query and indexing behavior, but preserving old search parameters without a retained resource or endpoint would not solve the main break.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The disappearing `ChargeItemDefinition` endpoint is the REST/API manifestation of the resource removal. It matters for route discovery and conformance tests, but endpoint aliases would require an explicit legacy resource policy and are not a cheap per-field compatibility fix.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This grouped behavior finding lists `ChargeItemDefinition`, but the actual compatibility judgment depends on each operation. It should be handled through operation-specific review and implementation CapabilityStatement guidance, not used as the main driver of this low-maturity resource-retirement conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource` behavior can affect systems that also process `ChargeItemDefinition` resources generically, but the assigned artifact is not `Resource` or `DomainResource`. It should not be double-counted as a ChargeItemDefinition-specific reason for resource-level migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is relevant background for generic search clients, but it is shared across `Resource` and `DomainResource`. For `ChargeItemDefinition`, the stronger and more specific search issue is that the resource-specific search surface disappears with the removed resource.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm an official R6 retirement/successor strategy for `ChargeItemDefinition`, including whether legacy instances should remain in an R4 island, a compatibility package, an incubator IG, or mapped into specific R6 artifacts.

Provide migration guidance for `applicability` and `propertyGroup` semantics, especially expression-based billing conditions and grouped price components, because these are central to the resource and not losslessly represented by the inspected R6 targets.

If `MonetaryComponent` is an intended migration target, define the R4 `deduction` to R6 `discount` policy explicitly, preferably with a ConceptMap or retained deprecated synonym so implementations do not invent incompatible billing-code mappings.

Document REST endpoint, search parameter, and `$apply` operation transition behavior together with the resource-retirement guidance so client generators and conformance suites know whether any legacy support is expected outside core R6.

caveats: No official R6 change rationale, Jira disposition, rendered narrative page, or ballot note was available in the local inputs.
No official cross-version StructureMap, ConceptMap, or compatibility extension package was available for `ChargeItemDefinition` migration.
The terminology comparison for price component codes used local CodeSystem evidence rather than full terminology-server value set expansions.
The R6 source is 6.0.0-ballot4; final published R6 content could change.
Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were considered as context only and were not scored as ChargeItemDefinition-specific breaks.
